phenotypes.label: Ischemic heart disease with risk factors
phenotypes.description: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease with acute and chronic ischemic presentations (angina, NSTEMI) alongside hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and hypertensive heart disease. Comorbid CKD stage 3A and systemic vascular disease (carotid obstruction, aortic ectasia) are frequent, with chest pain and abnormal cardiovascular studies noted.

phenotypes.label: Gastrointestinal bleeding and iron deficiency
phenotypes.description: Coherent gastrointestinal theme centered on bleeding and nutrient malabsorption with resultant iron deficiency anemia. Leading conditions include hemorrhoids, diverticulosis, colon polyps, gastritis/GERD, rectal bleeding, melena, and iron deficiency anemia due to blood loss. The pattern also includes inflammatory and structural GI disease such as celiac disease, inflammatory bowel disease, and postoperative abdominal complications (peritonitis, perforation, abscess).

phenotypes.label: Cardiometabolic risk and atherosclerosis
phenotypes.description: This cluster centers on essential hypertension and hyperlipidemia, accompanied by coronary atherosclerosis, valvular disease, edema, impaired glucose tolerance/type 2 diabetes, and cerebrovascular sequelae. It reflects a chronic cardiometabolic comorbidity baseline in routine care, skewing older and somewhat more male.

phenotypes.label: Hyperlipidemia with arrhythmias and GI disease
phenotypes.description: Cluster of older adults with cardiometabolic risk (hypercholesterolemia, impaired fasting glucose, hypertension) alongside atrial fibrillation/flutter, valvular disease, carotid disease, and ischemic stroke. Gastrointestinal conditions of aging are prominent, including GERD with Barrett’s esophagus, diverticular disease, internal hemorrhoids, and benign colon neoplasms. Skews older and somewhat more common in men.

phenotypes.label: Ocular disorders: cataract, glaucoma, dry eye
phenotypes.description: Cluster of ophthalmic conditions spanning age-related cataracts, refractive errors (myopia, presbyopia, astigmatism, hypermetropia), dry eye, and vitreoretinal disease (vitreous degeneration, epiretinal membrane, retinal detachment). It also includes glaucoma and ocular hypertension with other eye surface and inflammatory disorders (blepharitis, corneal ulcer, uveitis), reflecting patients with vision complaints and chronic eye disease.

phenotypes.label: Sleep disorders with anxiety/stress
phenotypes.description: Cluster of sleep–wake disorders (insomnia, hypersomnia, snoring) with prominent anxiety, adjustment and mild depressive symptoms, and fatigue. Neurobehavioral conditions such as ADHD and stress-related tachycardia appear alongside these complaints, reflecting a sleep disturbance and anxiety/stress spectrum. Overall, this represents patients presenting with combined sleep dysfunction and anxiety-related conditions.

phenotypes.label: BPH with LUTS and erectile dysfunction
phenotypes.description: Benign prostatic hyperplasia with lower urinary tract symptoms (nocturia, frequency, obstruction) and erectile dysfunction predominate, with raised PSA and testicular hypofunction also noted. Hearing loss and tinnitus are frequent co-recorded conditions, consistent with an older male population. This pattern is more common in males.

phenotypes.label: GI symptoms and IBD
phenotypes.description: Gastrointestinal presentations dominated by abdominal pain, nausea/vomiting, and diarrhea with epigastric and quadrant-specific pain. It concentrates inflammatory bowel disease (ulcerative colitis, Crohn’s) and complications such as abscess, fistula, and rectal bleeding, with related entities like gastroduodenitis, appendicitis, and primary sclerosing cholangitis. Functional and reflux disorders (IBS, GERD, esophagitis) also appear as co-occurring GI complaints.

phenotypes.label: Autoimmune rheumatologic disorders
phenotypes.description: Systemic autoimmune rheumatologic disease pattern featuring rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus, Sjögren’s syndrome, and inflammatory polyarthropathy, with extra‑articular/organ involvement such as episcleritis, sialoadenitis, interstitial lung disease, and lupus nephritis. Musculoskeletal pain and periarticular disorders (enthesopathy, rotator cuff and elbow tendinopathy, hip/hand/wrist pain) are prominent, and the burden is higher in females.

phenotypes.label: Thyroid and parathyroid disorders
phenotypes.description: Spectrum of thyroid and parathyroid disease, including hypothyroidism, goiter/nodules, autoimmune thyroiditis, postoperative hypothyroidism, and thyroid malignancy. Associated findings include neck mass and dysphonia, with hyperparathyroidism and hypocalcemia indicating parathyroid involvement. This pattern is more common in females.

phenotypes.label: Multiple sclerosis and related deficits
phenotypes.description: Neurologic phenotype marked by demyelinating CNS disease (multiple sclerosis/neuromyelitis optica) with sensory disturbance, weakness, ataxia, dysarthria, and gait impairment. Autonomic and visual involvement are prominent, with neurogenic bladder/bowel, optic atrophy, cranial nerve palsies, wheelchair dependence, and pressure ulcers; urinary tract infections are common from bladder dysfunction. Some patients have focal deficits from cerebrovascular injury (hemiplegia, cerebral hemorrhage).

phenotypes.label: Allergic rhinitis asthma and sinusitis
phenotypes.description: Allergic upper‑airway disease with asthma, centered on allergic rhinitis (including seasonal/pollen) alongside chronic/acute rhinitis and sinusitis, cough, and nasal congestion. Captures atopic patients with recurrent rhinosinusitis and variable asthma activity, with occasional ENT involvement such as otalgia or adenoid/turbinate hypertrophy.

phenotypes.label: Diabetes with nephropathy and vascular complications
phenotypes.description: Advanced type 2 diabetes with end‑organ damage: diabetic nephropathy/CKD (including ESRD and anemia), peripheral vascular disease with neuropathy, osteomyelitis and limb loss, and proliferative retinopathy with macular edema. Cardiorenal disease is prominent with coronary atherosclerosis, cardiomyopathy, and chronic/acute-on-chronic heart failure in the setting of hypertension. This pattern is more common in men and older adults.

phenotypes.label: Behavioral health, URIs, and injuries
phenotypes.description: Blend of mood and anxiety disorders, depression, ADHD and insomnia, together with acute respiratory infections (COVID-19, URIs, pharyngitis, otitis media) and minor trauma such as sprains, lacerations, and burns. This reflects general ambulatory complaints and injuries rather than a single disease process.

phenotypes.label: Pain, viral symptoms, common comorbidities
phenotypes.description: Mix of pain and nonspecific acute symptoms (chest pain, fever, cough, viral illness/COVID-19) alongside ubiquitous chronic conditions such as hypertension, dyslipidemia, obesity, GERD, and insomnia. Includes musculoskeletal pain and injuries (shoulder pain, radiculopathy, fracture) and general complaints, reflecting routine ambulatory and urgent care presentations.

phenotypes.label: Female breast cancer spectrum
phenotypes.description: Coherent cluster of female breast malignancy, spanning invasive and in‑situ disease, subsite codes, hormone‑receptor status, breast lumps, abnormal mammography/microcalcifications, and axillary nodal involvement. It also captures postoperative states and complications (acquired absence of breast, wound seroma) and sequelae such as lymphedema, with menopausal status and bone disorders commonly co‑coded. Predominantly seen in females.

phenotypes.label: HIV with hepatitis and opportunistic infections
phenotypes.description: Pattern of HIV/AIDS with opportunistic and infectious comorbidities, including herpes zoster, esophageal/skin candidiasis, Kaposi’s sarcoma, and recurrent cellulitis/abscesses. Co-infection with viral hepatitis (C and B) and other sexually transmitted infections (gonorrhea, genital herpes, anogenital warts) is prominent. This pattern is more common in males.

phenotypes.label: Colorectal malignancy with stoma complications
phenotypes.description: Pattern centers on lower gastrointestinal malignancies (rectum/anal canal) with postoperative status and ostomy, including stoma disorders or malfunction. Associated conditions include gastrointestinal and intra‑abdominal complications (paralytic ileus, GI bleeding, hemoperitoneum), acute blood‑loss anemia and hypovolemia, abdominal wall or incisional infection and abscess, gram‑negative sepsis, and pulmonary complications like atelectasis and pleural effusion.

phenotypes.label: Type 1 diabetes with complications
phenotypes.description: Type 1 diabetes with episodes of glycemic instability and metabolic decompensation, including hyperglycemia, hypoglycemia, acidosis, hyperosmolar states, dehydration, and acute kidney injury. Chronic microvascular and autonomic complications are prominent, such as retinopathy, proteinuria/microalbuminuria, gastroparesis, and peripheral circulatory or neuropathic involvement. Severe systemic illness like sepsis and respiratory failure appears in the context of decompensation.

phenotypes.label: Psoriatic arthritis with foot pain
phenotypes.description: Musculoskeletal symptoms centered on the feet and ankles (arthralgia, bilateral foot pain, plantar fascia involvement) occur alongside psoriasis and psoriatic arthropathy, consistent with psoriatic disease with enthesopathy. Additional joint pain and degenerative changes (hand/shoulder pain, osteoarthritis, spondylosis) reinforce a mixed inflammatory–degenerative musculoskeletal burden.

phenotypes.label: Bladder cancer and hematuria
phenotypes.description: Pattern centered on bladder pathology: bladder cancer, hematuria (microscopic and gross), cystitis, dysuria, and obstructive uropathy from stones with hydronephrosis. Pulmonary comorbidity is prominent (COPD, emphysema, dyspnea, oxygen dependence) along with vascular atherosclerosis, consistent with a smoking‑associated disease burden.

phenotypes.label: Mixed dermatology and urinary symptoms
phenotypes.description: The leading conditions blend benign dermatologic findings (actinic keratosis, melanocytic nevi, pruritic rashes, nail dystrophy) with urinary frequency and urgency plus miscellaneous primary‑care items like impacted cerumen. Other prominent conditions span unrelated systems (neurologic, gastrointestinal, musculoskeletal, ophthalmic, and genitourinary), so there is no single coherent clinical theme.

phenotypes.label: Inflammatory and follicular dermatoses
phenotypes.description: Dermatologic phenotype centered on inflammatory and follicular disorders: acne (including cystic and keloid forms), rosacea, seborrheic/contact/atopic dermatitis, folliculitis, and non-scarring alopecia, with pigmentary changes and benign cutaneous nevi. Represents common outpatient skin disease, including hidradenitis suppurativa and related follicular-occlusion conditions.

phenotypes.label: Gynecologic disorders with urinary symptoms
phenotypes.description: Female reproductive tract conditions dominate, including uterine fibroids, endometrial hyperplasia or carcinoma, endometriosis, cervicitis and vaginitis, ovarian cysts, and menopausal issues such as postmenopausal bleeding. These co-occur with lower urinary tract symptoms and infections (dysuria, mixed incontinence, UTI), with obesity, anemia, and GERD as common comorbidities.

phenotypes.label: Migraine and headache disorders
phenotypes.description: Primary headache disorders centered on migraine (with and without aura, chronic/intractable variants) and tension-type headache, often accompanied by dizziness/vertigo, nausea, and neck pain. Related entities such as posttraumatic headache, benign intracranial hypertension, and cervico‑occipital neuralgia appear in the same patients. Within this cohort it is more common in females and skews younger.

phenotypes.label: Type 2 diabetes with complications
phenotypes.description: Type 2 diabetes clustered with cardiometabolic comorbidities (hyperlipidemia, hypertension, obesity) and both poor- and well-controlled states. Prominent microvascular complications include neuropathy, nephropathy, and retinopathy, along with peripheral arterial disease and diabetic foot problems (calluses, onychomycosis, ulcers). This pattern is more common in men and older adults.

phenotypes.label: Sleep apnea with depression and PTSD
phenotypes.description: Cluster centered on obstructive sleep apnea and related sleep complaints, often alongside obesity. Prominent psychiatric comorbidity includes recurrent major depression and post‑traumatic stress disorder; ear symptoms (bilateral sensorineural hearing loss, tinnitus) and dental disease also appear. The pattern is more common in males.

phenotypes.label: Substance use with serious mental illness
phenotypes.description: Polysubstance use disorders (alcohol, opioids, cocaine, cannabis, stimulants) and nicotine dependence co-occur with serious mental illness, including bipolar disorder, schizophrenia/schizoaffective disorder, PTSD, and suicidal ideation. This pattern is more common in men and skews toward younger adults. Associated comorbidities include alcohol-related gastritis, dental disease, and minor injuries.

phenotypes.label: Epilepsy and intracranial pathology
phenotypes.description: Cluster of seizure and epilepsy presentations with associated neurologic manifestations such as loss of consciousness, syncope, amnesia, aphasia, and altered mental status. It concentrates intracranial etiologies and complications including encephalitis/meningitis, primary brain neoplasms and meningioma, traumatic brain injury with cerebral edema or skull base fracture, stroke with residual deficits, hydrocephalus, and aneurysmal disease.

phenotypes.label: Graves disease with ophthalmopathy
phenotypes.description: Pattern of hyperthyroidism, particularly Graves disease, with cardiac and ocular involvement. Features include thyrotoxicosis/toxic diffuse goiter with palpitations and arrhythmias, plus exophthalmos, diplopia, and ocular surface irritation consistent with thyroid eye disease.

phenotypes.label: Pulmonary embolism and DVT
phenotypes.description: Venous thromboembolism centered on pulmonary embolism, with dyspnea, chest pain, hypoxemia, and right heart strain (cor pulmonale/pulmonary hypertension). Includes lower‑extremity DVT, hypercoagulable states and thrombophilia, and complications such as pulmonary infarction and cardiogenic shock.

phenotypes.label: Acute multisystem symptoms
phenotypes.description: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea/constipation, and abdominal pain co-occur with dyspnea, wheezing, chest pain, generalized pain, anxiety, and nonspecific neurologic symptoms (syncope, tingling). This reflects nonspecific acute presentations across multiple organ systems rather than a single disease entity, typical of urgent or emergency visits. The pattern skews younger.

phenotypes.label: Myeloma with bone and renal disease
phenotypes.description: Multiple myeloma and related plasma cell dyscrasias with their complications dominate this cluster. Findings include anemia, hypercalcemia, pathologic vertebral fractures and collapse, and renal involvement with proteinuria, nephrotic/nephritic syndromes, and acute kidney injury. Amyloidosis, polyneuropathy, thrombocytopenia, and electrolyte disturbances appear as associated features.

phenotypes.label: Obesity and metabolic syndrome
phenotypes.description: Co-occurring obesity and metabolic syndrome features: morbid obesity with prediabetes/insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, essential hypertension, and hepatic steatosis. Associated conditions include obstructive sleep apnea, GERD, and vitamin D deficiency, with occasional bariatric surgery sequelae such as post‑surgical malabsorption.

phenotypes.label: Knee osteoarthritis and injuries
phenotypes.description: Cluster of degenerative and mechanical musculoskeletal conditions centered on the knee: osteoarthritis with bilateral knee pain, effusions, and related lower‑limb arthropathies. Frequently co-occurs with meniscal and ligamentous injuries, bursitis and tendinopathy, chondromalacia, and complications around joint prostheses including periprosthetic fracture.

phenotypes.label: Anxiety and depressive disorders
phenotypes.description: Mood and anxiety disorders dominate, including major depressive disorder (single and recurrent), generalized anxiety, panic disorder, PTSD, dysthymia, OCD, insomnia, and eating disorders. This reflects patients with primary psychiatric conditions, at times with somatic symptoms and occasional psychotic features. The pattern skews younger.

phenotypes.label: Pregnancy and gynecologic disorders
phenotypes.description: Female reproductive health centered on pregnancy and obstetric issues, including trimester care, high‑risk pregnancy, miscarriage, preterm labor, premature rupture of membranes, malpresentation, and anemia of pregnancy. Gynecologic conditions and fertility concerns co-appear, such as pelvic pain, ovarian cysts, polycystic ovary syndrome, vaginitis, irregular or heavy menses, and anovulatory infertility. Predominantly affects younger females.

phenotypes.label: Atrial fibrillation and movement disorders
phenotypes.description: This cluster mixes cardiac arrhythmias (paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, bradycardia, sick sinus syndrome) with central nervous system movement disorders (tremor, Parkinson’s disease, dyskinesia), gait instability, and immobility sequelae. The leading conditions span two unrelated systems without a single unifying clinical syndrome.

phenotypes.label: Degenerative spine with radiculopathy
phenotypes.description: Chronic axial spine disorders with radicular pain, centered on low back and neck pain, degenerative disc disease, spondylosis, and spinal stenosis. Features include sciatica and cervical radiculopathy, with related entities such as lumbago with sciatica, spondylolisthesis, and occasional neurologic complications (cauda equina, myelopathy).

phenotypes.label: Osteoporosis with osteoarthritis and fractures
phenotypes.description: Musculoskeletal and bone fragility pattern centered on osteoporosis and osteoarthritis, with osteoporotic fractures and tendon/soft‑tissue disorders (Achilles tendinitis, rotator cuff sprain, synovitis). Autoimmune rheumatic conditions such as seronegative rheumatoid arthritis and polymyalgia rheumatica also appear alongside age-related comorbidities (venous insufficiency, edema, hypothyroidism, vitamin D deficiency). This cluster is more common in older adults and in females.

phenotypes.label: Hematologic malignancy with cytopenias
phenotypes.description: Hematologic cancers—especially lymphomas—present with marrow suppression and infection complications. Leading conditions include neutropenia (often febrile), leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, pancytopenia, and anemia (including chemotherapy-related), with mucositis, rashes/eruptions, and viral infections also noted.

phenotypes.label: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma with immunodeficiency
phenotypes.description: Cluster of non-Hodgkin lymphomas with nodal and extranodal involvement (follicular, nodular, MALT), presenting with generalized and localized lymphadenopathy and systemic symptoms such as fatigue. Prominent immune defects and hypogammaglobulinemia indicate impaired humoral immunity in these patients, consistent with lymphoma-associated immunodeficiency.

phenotypes.label: Hepatobiliary-pancreatic and neuroendocrine tumors
phenotypes.description: Hepatobiliary and pancreatic malignancies cluster with gastrointestinal neuroendocrine (carcinoid) tumors, with frequent liver involvement (hepatocellular carcinoma, cholangiocarcinoma, liver metastases) and underlying cirrhosis, portal hypertension, and ascites. Associated symptom burden includes nausea, diarrhea, anorexia, and fatigue, with abnormal lung imaging and occasional procedure-related complications; treatment-induced polyneuropathy also appears.

phenotypes.label: Cancer with effusions and adenopathy
phenotypes.description: Lymphadenopathy with pleural and pericardial effusions, hemoptysis, chest pain, and dyspnea indicates thoracic involvement and systemic spread. Dysphagia, esophagitis, and oral cavity findings (tongue/parotid malignancies, painful mouth) co-occur, alongside hepatosplenomegaly and multiple nodules. Within the cancer cohort, this pattern skews slightly younger.

phenotypes.label: Prostate cancer with urinary complications
phenotypes.description: Prostate malignancy with PSA elevation and coexisting prostatic disease (BPH, prostatitis) presenting with lower urinary tract symptoms, obstruction, incontinence, and erectile dysfunction, including post‑prostatectomy changes. The pattern is concentrated in older men within the cancer cohort and includes nodal involvement of intrapelvic lymph nodes and lymphatic disorders.

phenotypes.label: Ovarian/testicular cancer with metastases
phenotypes.description: Gonadal malignancies (ovarian and testicular) with metastatic spread to intra‑abdominal/retroperitoneal lymph nodes, peritoneum, and lungs. Patients often have abdominopelvic masses, lymphadenopathy, pulmonary nodules or abnormal lung imaging, and obstructive uropathy (hydronephrosis); procedure‑related complications may also be recorded.

phenotypes.label: Cutaneous malignancy and photodamage
phenotypes.description: Dermatologic cancer pattern featuring squamous cell carcinoma, basal cell carcinoma, and melanoma with co‑occurring actinic/senile keratoses, dysplastic and melanocytic nevi, solar lentigines, and pigmentation changes. This reflects cutaneous malignancies accompanied by chronic photodamage and multiple pigmented lesions.

phenotypes.label: Mixed lung and ocular/skin conditions
phenotypes.description: This combines lower respiratory tract malignancy with evidence of prior lung resection alongside a dense cluster of ophthalmic disorders (cataract, age‑related macular degeneration, retinal vein occlusions) and periocular/sun‑exposed non‑melanoma skin cancers (basal and squamous cell of face, eyelid, ear). The pattern spans unrelated organ systems rather than one pathway and skews older within the cancer cohort.

phenotypes.label: Upper aerodigestive malignancies with dysphagia
phenotypes.description: Upper aerodigestive tract cancers involving the oropharynx, tonsil, base of tongue, larynx, and esophagus with prominent dysphagia, neck masses, and nodal metastases. Associated sequelae include ulcerative stomatitis (mucositis), salivary dysfunction, taste changes, lymphedema, and presence/complications of tracheostomy and gastrostomy tubes. Within the cancer cohort, this pattern is more common in males and skews older.

phenotypes.label: Cardiovascular disease in cancer patients
phenotypes.description: Cardiovascular comorbidity among cancer patients, centered on coronary atherosclerosis and prior myocardial infarction, chronic ischemic heart disease, and congestive heart failure. Rhythm and structural heart disease are prominent (atrial fibrillation, ventricular ectopy, cardiomyopathy, valvular stenosis/regurgitation, chamber enlargement), with occasional thoracic findings such as atelectasis, pleural thickening, consolidation, and pneumothorax.

phenotypes.label: Leukemia and bone marrow transplant
phenotypes.description: Hematologic malignancies centered on acute leukemias, chronic myeloid leukemia, and myelodysplastic syndromes, with hallmark cytopenias (anemia, thrombocytopenia, pancytopenia) and leukocytosis. Many patients have bone marrow transplant status with graft-versus-host disease and other transplant-related complications, alongside electrolyte disturbances and edema, with remission codes also appearing.

phenotypes.label: Melanoma and skin cancer
phenotypes.description: Cutaneous malignancies dominated by melanoma across head/neck, trunk, and extremity sites, with additional squamous cell carcinoma and general skin cancer codes. Lymph node involvement and secondary malignancy entries indicate nodal or metastatic spread in a subset. Within this cancer cohort, the pattern skews older.

phenotypes.label: Kidney cancer with CKD/absent kidney
phenotypes.description: Kidney and urinary tract malignancy with substantial chronic kidney disease burden and renal structural findings. Conditions include primary malignant neoplasm of kidney/urinary system, CKD stages (including hypertensive renal disease), renal mass/cyst, absent kidney/acquired absence, transplant status, hyperkalemia, and occasional postoperative complications. Within the cancer cohort, it is more common in males and skews older.

phenotypes.label: Cervical and colorectal cancer sequelae
phenotypes.description: Cervical and rectal malignancies with associated pelvic and anorectal conditions, including hemorrhoids, radiation proctitis, pelvic pain, dyspareunia, urinary tract infection/cystitis, and venous varices. Systemic effects such as anemia, immunosuppression/myelosuppression, and acute postoperative pain are also present, reflecting the pelvic cancer burden and its complications.

phenotypes.label: Lymphoma with neutropenia and infection
phenotypes.description: Lymphoid malignancies (Hodgkin and non‑Hodgkin lymphoma) with nodal involvement and systemic symptoms. Prominent are cytopenias and coagulopathy (anemia, drug‑induced neutropenia with neutropenic fever, low platelets) and infectious/inflammatory complications including pneumonia, fever, and SIRS; imaging abnormalities and lymphadenopathy are frequent. A subset shows second primary cancers or transplant status.

phenotypes.label: Lung cancer with pleural disease
phenotypes.description: Primary lung malignancy with prominent pleural involvement and respiratory symptoms, including dyspnea, cough, pleural effusion, atelectasis, and abnormal chest imaging. COPD/emphysema and pleural complications are frequent comorbid features, and the pattern skews older within the cancer cohort.

phenotypes.label: ET and PV myeloproliferative neoplasms
phenotypes.description: Myeloproliferative neoplasms centered on essential thrombocythemia and polycythemia vera, with associated erythrocytosis and thrombocytosis. Some patients also have iron overload disorders and liver malignancy, but the dominant pattern is a clonal hematologic cancer phenotype. Within this cancer cohort it is relatively more common in males.

phenotypes.label: Nonmelanoma skin cancer with photodamage
phenotypes.description: Cutaneous malignancies dominated by basal and squamous cell carcinoma across the face, trunk, and extremities, with concurrent actinic keratoses and chronic phototoxic changes. Includes neoplasms of uncertain behavior and melanocytic nevi, reflecting extensive sun‑damaged skin under surveillance for cancer. Within this subgroup, it skews older and is more common in males.

phenotypes.label: Neuroendocrine and adrenal-pituitary cancers
phenotypes.description: Cluster centered on neuroendocrine malignancies with carcinoid syndrome and endocrine organ involvement, including adrenal and pituitary tumors with hypopituitarism. Colon cancer appears alongside gastrointestinal conditions such as diverticular disease and reflux, with neurofibromatosis type 1 and peripheral/autonomic nerve tumors also represented. Within the cancer cohort, this pattern skews older.

phenotypes.label: Metastatic cancer and complications
phenotypes.description: Advanced malignancy with widespread metastatic involvement and substantial symptom burden. Signals include lung, soft tissue, oral cavity, and bone primaries with metastases to bone, brain, pleura, and intrathoracic nodes, malignant ascites, cancer pain, anemia, malnutrition, and constipation. Postoperative and radiation-related conditions, drug eruptions, and internal jugular vein thrombosis reflect treatment sequelae.
